description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace" to hold intermediate results.  
2. Recursively enumerate all entries under /working and record each path whose filename is exactly "workspace" together with its file-type metadata into a file named "matches.txt" inside "temp_workspace".  
3. From "matches.txt", filter and save only the entries identified as regular files into "regular_matches.txt" inside "temp_workspace".  
4. Check accessibility of each path in "regular_matches.txt", remove any duplicates, and write the final list and its count to "regular_count.txt" inside "temp_workspace".  
5. Prepare a summary file named "decision_prepare.txt" in "temp_workspace" that states whether the count in "regular_count.txt" is greater than zero and is ready to be used to output the final "yes" or "no" decision.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Create a temporary duplicate of the /working directory named 'temp_workspace' and confirm the duplication completed without errors.
2. Recursively enumerate every filesystem entry inside 'temp_workspace' and save one path per line to a file named 'file_list.txt'.
3. From 'file_list.txt', select entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and for each candidate verify it is a regular file, writing confirmed paths to 'matches.txt'.
4. Inspect 'matches.txt' and write a single status marker to 'existence_flag': write 'exists' if at least one path is present, otherwise write 'absent'; also log any multiple matches to 'duplicates.log'.
5. Prepare a file named 'final_output.txt' that contains the single word corresponding to the status marker ('yes' if 'existence_flag' is 'exists', otherwise 'no'), but do not display it and leave temporary artifacts intact for verification.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold all intermediate records and results.  
2. Obtain a recursive inventory of all entries under /working and save the raw output to "temp_workspace_check/raw_listing.txt".  
3. From "raw_listing.txt", extract all entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and write those full paths to "temp_workspace_check/candidates.txt".  
4. For each path in "candidates.txt", verify that the path refers to a regular file (not a directory, symlink, or special file) and record only the confirmed regular-file paths into "temp_workspace_check/verified_workspace_files.txt", removing any non-regular entries.  
5. Create "temp_workspace_check/summary.txt" that states whether "verified_workspace_files.txt" is non-empty and prepare that summary for the final decision step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" and inside it create a file named "search_results.txt" to record findings.
2. Recursively traverse /working and record every filesystem entry named "workspace" (with full paths) into "search_results.txt".
3. Filter "search_results.txt" to retain only paths that refer to regular files, overwriting the file with this filtered list.
4. Verify each retained path still exists as a regular file, remove any stale or duplicate entries, and ensure "search_results.txt" reflects the final verified set (possibly empty).
5. Prepare a single-line result based on "search_results.txt": "yes" if it contains at least one verified regular-file path, otherwise "no", but do not output the result yet.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
